claim: RTL-SDR devices are commonly recommended as the entry-level SDR hardware for student GNU Radio projects (FM receiver, ADS-B, DSP/FFT lessons) because they are low-cost and receive-only, but cannot transmit and use an 8-bit ADC with limited bandwidth.
stance_target: typical hardware progression for student SDR/GNU Radio projects
scope_conditions: vendor buying-guide, not peer-reviewed; reflects common industry/hobbyist practice rather than an authoritative standard
quoted_support: RTL-SDR Blog V3 or V4 USB-C is usually the best GNU Radio beginner SDR because it is affordable, receive-only, widely supported, and good for first flowgraphs such as FM reception, ADS-B, FFT displays, filters, and demodulation.

claim: USRP hardware (B210/X310) with the UHD software ecosystem is the commonly cited choice for research-grade GNU Radio wireless communications labs, including MIMO testbeds and private 5G/O-RAN experimentation.
stance_target: hardware tier appropriate for advanced/graduate ECE wireless research projects
scope_conditions: vendor buying-guide; low independent authority but reflects common academic SDR lab practice
quoted_support: USRP hardware is one of the strongest choices for serious GNU Radio research because it has a mature UHD ecosystem, broad research adoption, and strong support in university and laboratory environments.
